faq.q: What are good things to ponder?
faq.a: Good things to ponder are questions without quick answers that touch how you live, like where your best energy goes, what you could let go of, and what “enough” means to you.

faq.q: What is the difference between pondering and overthinking?
faq.a: Pondering is slow, open, and usually leads to insight or action. Overthinking loops on the same worry without moving forward.

faq.q: How long should I spend reflecting?
faq.a: Twenty to thirty minutes is plenty for one question. You can always return to it later in the week.

faq.q: Should I write down my reflections?
faq.a: Writing helps many people slow their thoughts and notice patterns. Even a few lines in a notebook can make your thinking clearer.

faq.q: What if I don’t find an answer?
faq.a: That’s normal. Some questions are meant to be lived with for a while, and answers often show up later when you’re not looking for them.

faq.q: Why is the weekend a good time to ponder?
faq.a: Weekends usually offer more unstructured time and fewer interruptions. That space lets your mind shift out of task mode into deeper thinking.
